basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 20-21.' and it opens 'Vers. 20, 21. Reptile animae viventis. Reptilia pisces hoc loco accipe. Mutabilem animam'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: Vers. 20, 21. Reptile animae viventis. Reptilia pisces hoc loco accipe. Mutabilem animam [Vulg., motabilem an. ] dicit animalium ad comparationem hominis. Quia licet mortalis sit homo ad comparationem Dei, tamen immortalis est ad comparationem caeterorum animalium, qua parte imaginem Dei retinet.
